svg.aria-label: A pinout for a thirty-way flexible cable connector on a display module. Across the top the connector is drawn as it physically is, one straight row of thirty pads, each filled with the colour of its category: ink for ground, gold for power rails, blue for the ten pads that form five differential pairs, and green for control and I2C lines. Square brackets above the row join each differential pair and name it, so the two halves of a pair can never be read as unrelated pins. A triangle marks pin one at the left end, with a note that the real part carries the same triangle in silkscreen. Below the strip, a two-column table lists all thirty pins with number, colour dot, signal name and a short note. Under the table an orange warning box states the trap this figure exists to prevent: left and right depend on which face you are looking at, a drawing seen from the component side is the mirror image of the same connector seen from the pad side, so a pinout without a stated viewing side and a pin one marker is not usable. Closing notes add that differential pairs must be bracketed rather than merely listed, that the ground pins sitting between pairs are shields and not spare grounds, and that this pinout is an example rather than a part number, so the panel datasheet remains the authority
svg.font-family: Poppins, 'Noto Sans SC', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: PINOUT · 30-WAY PANEL FLEX, AS THE PART IS ACTUALLY BUILT
the strip is the physical row of pads; the table below is what each one carries. one without the other is not a pinout.
the trap this figure exists to prevent
left and right depend on which face you are looking at. seen from the component side, this connector is the mirror of itself seen from the pad side.
so a pinout is only usable when it states the viewing side and marks pin 1 — and the part itself has to carry that mark too, or the drawing cannot be checked.
bracket · the two halves of one differential pair
the pairs are bracketed, not merely listed. a pair split across two table rows reads as two independent pins — and routing them that way is how a lane fails at the far end of the flex.
the grounds sitting between pairs are shields, not spare grounds — reassigning one of them to something else changes the impedance of the pair next to it.
this is an example arrangement, not a part number. the panel datasheet is the authority for any board you are actually building.
